info.title: Notra API
info.description: OpenAPI schema for Notra content endpoints. Use GET /v1/status for public reachability. Error responses include recovery guidance. Breaking changes ship under a new major path; deprecated operations send Deprecation and Sunset headers at least 90 days before removal.

externalDocs.description: Notra API versioning and deprecation policy

tags.name: Feedback
tags.description: Collect and triage feedback submitted by AI agents. Agents post to the organization's feedback URL without credentials; reading and triage require an API key with feedback.read or feedback.write.

tags.name: GEO
tags.description: Manage generative engine optimization: projects, tracking settings, prompts, prompt sequences, competitors, scans, visibility reads, content gaps and briefs, agent readiness and AI traffic. Project-scoped endpoints require the GEO plan entitlement in addition to their scope; organization-level ingest endpoints require only the traffic scope.

tags.name: Sites
tags.description: Notra Sites are hosted blogs and changelogs built from a GitHub repository. Read Sites and their deployments, start builds, preview posts on a Site, open pull requests that publish posts to it, and manage blog.json authors and the author page through staged Design changes. Domains, settings, rollbacks and deletion stay in the dashboard.

BearerAuth.description: Send your API key in the Authorization header as Bearer API_KEY. Account API keys work in every workspace you belong to: send X-Notra-Organization-Id with the workspace id or slug to choose one. Workspace endpoints require it when you belong to more than one workspace; GET /v1/me/workspaces works without it. Organization keys only accept their own workspace there.

patch.description: Updates any combination of title, slug, markdown, status, and metadata. Sending markdown re-renders the stored HTML, and when title is omitted it is taken from the first heading in the markdown, keeping the existing title when the markdown has no heading. Slugs and metadata are only accepted for blog posts and changelogs. Inside metadata, send only the fields you want to change; tags and authorIds replace the stored list, and authorIds must come from GET /v1/posts/authors. A blog post that publishes to a Notra Sites site can also credit that site's authors as site:<id>, the ref from GET /v1/sites/{siteId}/authors. Title, slug, markdown, or metadata updates also sync a post linked to GitHub: an open pull request gets a new commit, and a repository set to publish directly gets a direct commit when its live branch allows one (unprotected, file unchanged on GitHub). Otherwise, including closed or merged pull requests, GitHub is left as is and no new pull request is opened; the post is still saved. GitHub sync errors occur after saving the post: 429 includes Retry-After, 502 indicates a sync error, and 504 indicates an unknown sync outcome. Check the PR before retrying an unconfirmed sync.

post.summary: Run a GEO prompt sequence now
post.description: Runs the sequence now. API-based answer engines run synchronously: the request stays open while every turn plays against each of them, which can take several minutes, and `checks`, `mentions` and `engines` report their result. Tracked consumer apps (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, AI Mode, Copilot) answer far more slowly, so they are queued as a background scan instead: `queuedScanId` names it and `queuedEngines` lists the apps it covers. Poll `GET /v1/projects/{projectId}/geo/scans/{scanId}` for that part. A run with only consumer apps answers right away with `checks: 0`. Runs also work while automatic scans are paused. Use a client timeout of at least five minutes; after four minutes the API stops waiting and answers 409 while the run finishes on its own. Do not retry; read the result from the project's GEO checks. The work happens inside the Notra dashboard, which owns the model credentials and billing gates; the public API never calls an answer engine itself. Results also land in the project's GEO checks.
